flags: Unvaried slot: 'mechanism' = transit-timing-method in all 8 hypotheses — no rival detection mechanism (e.g., photographic, radar, visual) appears anywhere in the frontier, so this assumption is structurally unexamined by the whole population.

Over-narrow clustering around the anchor: alpha-observatory appears in 7/8 hypotheses, comet-q in 7/8, alpha-team in 5/8, and action='sighted' in 6/8 — the frontier is a radial one-slot ablation of a single base claim rather than a spread of independently plausible hypotheses.

No dissenting reading anywhere: all 7 non-anchor hypotheses have d=0 and u=1.0. Uncertainty here means 'no evidence yet gathered,' not 'evidence found that disagrees.' A per-hypothesis critic sees each as merely uninformative but misses that this is true of the ENTIRE non-anchor population simultaneously — generation has produced breadth of claims without any accompanying evidence search, so the frontier cannot currently distinguish 'alternatives are false' from 'alternatives were never checked.'

Interval is confounded with anchor status: the only hypothesis with a narrow, informative interval [1950,1950] is also the only one with strong belief (b=0.75); every other hypothesis (including ones that otherwise match the anchor's slots) reverts to the maximally wide [1900,1999]. No hypothesis isolates interval by pairing the anchor's exact actor/action/object/place/mechanism with a wide or alternate-narrow interval, so it's impossible to attribute the anchor's support specifically to temporal precision versus its other fixed slots.

Purely single-slot perturbation design: no hypothesis varies two or more slots together (e.g., beta-team at beta-observatory), so interaction effects between slots are entirely unexplored — generation appears to have stopped at first-order ablation and is not combining or recombining variations.

Atomicity (a) values differ substantially in the unevaluated set (0.18 for unverified-observer vs 0.62–0.88 for others) but this signal is not yet linked to any belief/disbelief mass — worth checking whether low-atomicity actors are being systematically deprioritized for evidence search rather than genuinely tested.
recommended_actions: Widen: introduce hypotheses that vary 'mechanism' (e.g., photographic-plate-method, radar-echo-method) to test whether transit-timing-method is genuinely best-supported or simply never challenged.

Split: add a hypothesis identical to the anchor on actor/action/object/place/mechanism but with the wide interval [1900,1999] (and/or alternate narrow intervals near 1950) to isolate the interval variable's actual contribution to the anchor's high belief.
Recombine: generate multi-slot perturbations (e.g., beta-team + beta-observatory, or other-actor + other-object) to probe interaction effects instead of relying solely on one-slot-at-a-time ablation.

Generalize/evidence pass: run an evidence-gathering step against the 7 u=1.0 hypotheses before the next generation round — convert at least some to b>0 or d>0 so the frontier contains at least one genuine dissenting (higher-d) reading rather than uniform total uncertainty.

Investigate the atomicity disparity for unverified-observer (a=0.18) — confirm whether this reflects a real source-reliability judgment or a placeholder default, and ensure it isn't silently suppressing that branch from being explored further.
response.summary: The 8-hypothesis frontier is a single anchor (alpha-team sighted comet-q at alpha-observatory via transit-timing-method, interval=[1950,1950], b=0.75/u=0.25) surrounded by seven pure one-slot-at-a-time perturbations, each carrying u=1.0/b=0/d=0 (i.e., unevaluated, not actually disconfirmed). This is a classic ablation sweep around a single base claim rather than a genuinely diverse hypothesis population: coverage is heavily skewed toward the anchor's slot values, one slot is never touched at all, interval is confounded with the anchor, and no alternative has been evidentially tested — so there is literally no dissenting/contradicting reading anywhere in the frontier.
